quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding, you should wear boots or shoes that:

options.text: Cover your ankles.
Have long heels.
Have long and loose laces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Riding boots should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Check your safety before riding. Test each brake control to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: Which material gives riders the best protection?

options.text: Fleece
Leather
Denim

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's transmission must be in neutral before you start the engine. A neutral indicator light on the speedometer shows when the motorcycle is in neutral.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: As your motorcycle increases speed, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle goes faster, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
You heard a loud noise.
A discharge of air can be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Riding alongside a vehicle in the next lane is:

options.text: Discouraged because it may put you in the other vehicle's blind spot.
Encouraged if you want to travel at the same speed as the other driver.
Acceptable if you want to race the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discouraged because it may put you in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The other vehicle also blocks your escape route if you need to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: As a rider, how can you reduce your chance of having an accident?

options.text: Don't look ahead for hazards.
Don't use turn signals because they might distract other drivers.
Make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make yourself visible, signal your turns clearly, keep distance between you and other vehicles, look ahead at the road, and identify hazards. Always be ready to react to anything dangerous.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Stare straight ahead at the road directly in front of the motorcycle.
Refuse to move to avoid a possible hazard.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead on the road. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: Parking is not allowed.
It marks the right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows where the right edge of a traffic lane is.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like car mirrors.
No, they do not have blind spots.
Mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like car mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is true about wind noise when riding?

options.text: It is easy to get used to.
It can cause permanent hearing damage.
It is never dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear proper ear plugs or hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: When cars are entering from an on-ramp, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Assume the entering drivers can see them.
Never assume the entering drivers can see them.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the entering drivers can see them.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Don't assume drivers see you. Change lanes away from the entering traffic if you can. If you can't change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If a rider wears a helmet during a crash, are they more likely to survive?

options.text: No, they are less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
No, they have the same chance as someone without a helmet.
Yes, they are more likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are more likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders with helmets, no matter how fast they are going.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Leave the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse by encouraging them to tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: Are footrests required on a motorcycle?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share the same footrests.
Yes, they are required for both the driver and passenger.
No, they are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are required for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. The motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing helps prevent your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely and go only when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, look for other traffic or pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Long pants
Gloves
A baseball cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: When riding a motorcycle, wear protective clothing. Good protective gear includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, over-the-ankle closed-toe boots, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible when riding.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as on your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding it in a safe, controlled area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Recommended because it blocks the wind.
Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane without knowing you are there.

questions.question: Having just one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your blood alcohol is below the legal limit.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: Pull off the road after hitting an object. Check your tires and rims for damage before continuing. Make sure nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt.
